producer_report.summary:
The reader, producer and verifier now each have an explicit model and effort in athena.toml. Both reach the claude driver and appear on every invocation record. A reading that marks a job hard gets a stronger producer setting, with the reason recorded, and `athena status` shows the three measures per producer model and effort. I ran the full `cargo test --locked` once. It exited without a failure code, but the output was too large to read in full, so I could not confirm the pass counts. Clippy and fmt --check are clean.

- **Config:** `[models]` has `reader_effort`, `producer_effort`, `verifier_effort` (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`), plus `hard_producer_model` and `hard_producer_effort`. Unknown effort values are rejected, as is a hard model outside `producer_allowed`. A file without the keys reads as `medium`.
- **Driver and records:** the claude driver passes `--effort` next to `--model`. `Invocation` has an optional `effort`, so older records still load. `Reading` has optional `hard_reason` and `producer_effort`.
- **Escalation:** the reader's output has a `hard_reason` field, null or a sentence. When it is non-blank, the reading takes the hard producer setting and records the reason and effort, and the run applies that effort to the producer. An ordinary or blank reading keeps the default and records neither.
- **Status:** `producer_settings` groups dispatched jobs by their first producer invocation's model and effort. It gives the first-pass verification rate, landed share and cost per landed job, and shows `n/a` where nothing landed or was verified. Records without effort go into an "unrecorded" bucket.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG.md notes that request 20261013-042934-a1j8 is absorbed. docs/decisions.md has D136 with alternatives, including dropping the planner and critic because planning is off. docs/records.md also documents the new record fields.
- **Shipped setting:** the hard producer setting is the same model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) at effort `high`, against `medium` by default. There is no stronger allowed model, because the verifier's model may not produce.

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test drain -- hard_reading every_role
checks_run.note: 2 tests: hard versus ordinary reading, and every role's model and effort on its record

checks_run.command: cargo test --locked -p athena-data -p athena-agent -p athena-core -p athena-cli --lib effort

Full suite run once; the command returned no failure exit code. Output was too large to read and the saved file was outside the allowed directory, so pass counts were not reviewed.

criteria_check.evidence: claude::tests::the_model_and_effort_of_an_invocation_reach_the_command_line checks `--model` and `--effort` values in ClaudeCodeDriver::command_line. invocation::tests::the_record_names_the_model_and_effort_the_invocation_ran_with checks the record's effort. The drain test every_role_runs_at_its_configured_model_and_effort_and_the_record_names_both checks the reader, verifier and producer records against the config. The first two plus the drain tests passed when run.

criteria_check.criterion: A test (cargo test) shows a reading marking a job hard gets the stronger producer model or effort with its reason recorded, while an ordinary reading keeps the configured default and records no escalation reason.

It checks a hard reading's producer model, effort and reason on the reading and the producer's invocation record. It also checks that null and blank readings keep haiku, the configured effort and no reason.

Both passed.

open_issues: That claude 2.1.302 accepts `--effort` with the levels low, medium, high, xhigh and max was not verified, because no agent was run.
The hard-job rule reaches the reader only through the `hard_reason` field description in the output schema; no reader prompt text was added.
Planner and critic invocations get the verifier's effort via the role fallback; they are not separately configured because planning is off.
I could not read the full test output, so the pass counts of the full `cargo test --locked` run are unreviewed.
mistakes: While changing the reading fixture in reading.rs with a broad replace, I first missed the real construction in `build_reading` and fixed it right after; no lasting effect.
I did not add a line about hard jobs to the reader prompt; the guidance rests on the output schema's field description.
learnings: `Reading`, `Invocation` and `AgentInvocation` are built as literals in many tests, so a new field costs one edit per site; optional serde fields keep old records loadable.
The reader's schema is generated from `ReadingOutput`. `harden` makes every field required in the JSON schema, while `#[serde(default)]` keeps parsing lenient for scripted test readings.
Config changes feed `Config::reading_inputs`, so adding `[models]` keys changes the config digest used for readings.
The verifier's model may not be in `producer_allowed`, so the hard producer setting cannot use a model stronger than the default producer; the shipped escalation is a higher effort.
The Fixture in `crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs` builds its config from the repository's athena.toml, so config changes reach those end-to-end tests.
desires: Read access to the saved large tool-output file, so a full-suite result could be inspected after the run.
